correctness.rationale: Rechecked the marked-process claim in /workspace/repairs/5/RESULT.md. From G=1+U_(i+1)−U_i, the tail triangle has area δ²/2; consecutive exceedances at δ≤1/2 require incompatible values of the shared uniform. Nonadjacent indices use disjoint uniforms. Thus for fixed L and sufficiently large n the one-point mark density is exactly t/n on [0,L]. For a nonnegative compactly supported continuous f, h_i=E[1−exp(−f(i/n,T_i))]≤L²/(2n). The finite Laplace product expansion equals the product for independent entries except for subsets with neighboring indices. Charging their absolute contributions to an adjacent pair gives bound exp(sum h_i) sum_i h_i h_(i+1)=O_L(n^−1); the independent product then converges by a Riemann sum to the Poisson Laplace functional with intensity ds t dt. This directly proves the vague convergence for the actual spatial grid and deficit normalization. On bounded mark windows the ordering is continuous in the absence of ties or cutoff points, which holds almost surely in the limit; letting the cutoff grow captures each fixed rank. Product intensity makes the minimum location uniform independent of its mark, and the kth survival is the Poisson count probability below t for mean t²/2. Boundaries have scaled length at most one, while floor(n/2) disjoint internal pairs independently beat one with probability 1/2. The contextual finite law is correct: only independent subsets contribute moments, variance subtracts twice the adjacent q² covariance, and z=0 uses a threshold ≥3/2 so endpoints cannot exceed it. Independently evaluated the n=10, δ=1/3 example with rational arithmetic, giving 1097009/1889568=0.5805607419261969.
